record.original_question: Let mu be a nonnegative continuous majorant on [-1,1], and let omega_mu in P_n be the associated snake polynomial, meaning the unique degree-n polynomial that oscillates most between plus and minus mu at an alternation set. Find a class of majorants mu for which the associated snake polynomials Q_n have a Chebyshev expansion Q_n = sum_{i=0}^n a_i T_i whose coefficients are either all nonnegative or strictly sign-alternating, in the sense that a_i a_{i+1} < 0 for every i.

evidence.quote: Consider a majorant mu in C[-1, 1], mu(x) >= 0, x in [-1, 1]. If there exists P in Pn, P != 0, such that -mu(x) <= P(x) <= mu(x), x in [-1, 1], then there exists a unique polynomial omega_mu in Pn called snake polynomial associated with mu, which oscillates most between plus and minus mu.

Open problem. Find a class of majorants mu for which the associated snake polynomials Qn have non-negative or sign alternating expansion in the Chebyshev polynomials of the first kind, i.e. Qn = sum_{i=0}^n a_i T_i with all a_i >= 0 or with a_i a_{i+1} < 0 for all i.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $\mathcal{P}_n$ denote the space of real polynomials of degree at most $n$, and let $T_i(x) = \cos(i \arccos x)$ be the Chebyshev polynomial of the first kind of degree $i$ on $[-1,1]$.

A nonnegative continuous function $\mu \in C[-1,1]$ with $\mu(x) \geq 0$ is called a majorant. Suppose there exists a nonzero $P \in \mathcal{P}_n$ such that $-\mu(x) \leq P(x) \leq \mu(x)$ for all $x \in [-1,1]$. Then there is a unique polynomial $\omega_\mu \in \mathcal{P}_n$, called the snake polynomial associated with $\mu$, which "oscillates most" between $+\mu$ and $-\mu$: there exist points $-1 \leq x_0 < x_1 < \cdots < x_n \leq 1$ such that $\omega_\mu(x_k) = (-1)^{n-k}\varepsilon\,\mu(x_k)$ for some fixed sign $\varepsilon \in \{-1,+1\}$, and $\omega_\mu$ is extremal with respect to this alternation property.

Write the Chebyshev expansion
$$\omega_\mu(x) = \sum_{i=0}^{n} a_i\, T_i(x).$$

Identify a class of majorants $\mu$ on $[-1,1]$ for which, for every admissible $n$, the coefficients $(a_i)_{i=0}^{n}$ of the associated snake polynomial $\omega_\mu$ satisfy one of the following:
(i) $a_i \geq 0$ for all $0 \leq i \leq n$; or
(ii) $a_i\, a_{i+1} < 0$ for all $0 \leq i \leq n-1$ (strictly sign-alternating).
artifact.status_search_result: The question is explicitly posed as an open problem in the source where snake polynomials are studied, and a web search yields no published resolution; standard references on Chebyshev polynomials do not address this specific question about snake polynomials having nonnegative or sign-alternating Chebyshev coefficients.

status_evidence.claim: No standard reference discusses or resolves the sign structure of Chebyshev coefficients of snake polynomials.

status_evidence.snippet: Comprehensive treatise on Chebyshev polynomials that does not address snake-polynomial Chebyshev-coefficient sign patterns.
status_evidence.claim: The problem is not addressed in standard treatises on Chebyshev polynomials.
